title: I.2: Fugue in C minor

groocock.chapter: 7 Group 2: Fugues for Three Voices, without Stretto

entries.notes: CS leaps up a third instead of a tenth (octave interchange for the latter part)
extended to cadence; first chord of bar 27 is VI instead of iv
in the coda over tonic pedal, tierce de Picardie at end

episodes.material: first five notes of the subject (fourth widened to a sixth) with upward scale inverting the C1 opening
two-part canon on the opening subject figure, running bass developing falling scale of C1
inverts bass of ep.2 in the soprano; thirds in lower voices from C2 (bar 8); suggestion of bVII and iv on the way
17-18 interchange at the twelfth of episode 1 with subject figure in tenths; 18-20 interchange at the fifteenth
22-25 repeat of episode 2 with upper voices interchanged; 25-26 allusion to episode 1
episodes.sequence: falling sequence in bass intersecting rising sequence in soprano

countersubjects.interchange: fifteenth (latter part also at octave, bar 15)
countersubjects.notes: C1 downward scale affects tonality of every entry; C2 first in middle voice bars 7-8, could be mistaken for a free part; its figure (first four notes of bar 8) provides material for the episode at bar 13; five of six permutations of the three lines used (not C1 bass / subject middle / C2 soprano)

subject.notes: dominant occurs shortly after the opening; subject unvaried in all six entries; differs in one small detail from subject (p.2)

key_plan: Group 2 table: Exp i v EP i | Dev EP III EP v EP i | Final EP i i

claims.claim: Episodic fugue without stretto, contrasted with I.1 (stretto fugue without episodes).
Very minimum of modulation: apart from two bars in III, everything in i or v.
C1 scale forms the basis of all five episodes, direct or inverted.
Second CS figure in bar 8 supplies the two lower voices for the whole episode beginning at bar 13.
Episode 4: interchange at the twelfth then at the fifteenth.
Bach uses five of the six permutations of subject and two CS.
Exposition contains an episode (bars 5-6) before the third entry.
